case.case_title: Abasin Banda v. S. I. Gunaratne & Others

clause.text: Any person detained shall be brought before a judge and cannot be held without legal order.

case_context.legal_issue: Whether the petitioner was produced before a judge without unnecessary delay as required by Article 13(2).
case_context.petitioner_claim: The petitioner claimed there was an unreasonable delay in producing him before the Magistrate, violating Article 13(2).
case_context.respondent_argument: The respondents did not dispute the production timing but argued the arrest and detention were lawful.
key_facts: Petitioner was arrested at about 6 p.m. on 1 March 1995 and produced before the Magistrate the next morning on 2 March 1995.
There was no lawful ground for arrest, making the detention unreasonable.
The 24-hour limit for production is the maximum allowed by law.
The petitioner was assaulted while in custody.

reasoning.interpretation_summary: Article 13(2) requires that any person detained be brought before a judge without unnecessary delay, with a maximum limit of 24 hours exclusive of travel time. Detention beyond what is reasonable under the circumstances violates this right.
reasoning.application_to_facts: Since there were no grounds for arrest, the overnight detention was unreasonable. The failure to produce the petitioner before the Magistrate soon after arrest violated the procedure established by law and Article 13(2).
principles_established: Unreasonable delay in producing detainees before a judge violates Article 13(2).
The 24-hour limit is the maximum time for production before a Magistrate.
Detention without lawful grounds is inherently unreasonable.
precedents_cited: Mahinda Rajapakse & Vasudeva Nanayakkara v. Chief Inspector Karunaratne & Others

outcome.holding: The court declared that the petitioner’s fundamental right under Article 13(2) was violated by the 1st respondent due to unreasonable delay in producing him before a judge.
outcome.remedy_or_orders: Declaration of violation of Article 13(2) rights; compensation awarded as part of overall relief.

link_explanation.why_this_clause_matters: Article 13(2) is central to the court’s reasoning on the unlawfulness of the detention period and the failure to produce the petitioner before a judge without unnecessary delay.

evidence.evidence_excerpt: The petitioner was arrested at about 6 p.m. and produced before the Magistrate only the next morning, with no lawful grounds for arrest, making the detention unreasonable and violating Article 13(2).
